div.div:
ădumbrātim , adv. adumbro,
I.sketched in shadow, à la silhouette, in general or in outline (opp. adamussim): “quasi adumbratim paulum simulata videntur,” as it were covered with shadows, dimly resembling, Lucr. 4, 363 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
